about: The specimens the simulated microscope can mount and their targets (labelled structures), BSD-3-Clause. One registry for the engine (cli, viewer, webSMLM) and Micro-Manager: tools/gen_dye_library.mjs builds it into the C++ (DyeLibraryData.inc) and the JS (dye_library_data.js, web/dye_library.js). A target's 'prefix' names its engine options (<prefix>-dye, <prefix>-mode, <prefix>-label-pct, ...) and 'structure' its core structure id (ISC_STRUCT_*); its typical labels per mode are in data/dyes/library.json typicalLabels; 'defaultDye' (optional, a dye id or 'None') = the default of <prefix>-dye when not the typical dye ('None': the target is off until labelled). 'paint' = its DNA-PAINT binding kinetics (a property of the docking/imager sequence, not of the dye): konPerMPerSec (imager association rate, /M/s; binding events per site per second = k_on x c) and onSec (mean bound time, exponential; half-time = ln 2 x onSec), the defaults of <prefix>-paint-kon and <prefix>-paint-on-sec; imagerNm = the default imager concentration (nM, <prefix>-imager-nm). A new target: its core geometry, an entry here, its typical labels. A new specimen: its core generator, an entry here, a Micro-Manager device (spec/MM_DEVICES.md). The engine's 'specimen' option is the index here (core param 'specimen').

specimens.name: Cell field
specimens.notes: Adherent cells packed on a coverslip: cytoplasm, nucleus, microtubules, nuclear pore complexes and the nuclear lamina on the nuclear envelope (core/).

paint.notes: k_on: order of magnitude of 9-10 nt imagers (estimate; faster with optimized sequences, schueder2019). onSec 0.05 s (half-time 35 ms) keeps the pre-issue-16 default look (estimate); 9 nt docking strands bind for ~0.3-1 s. imagerNm 1 nM: about the emitters per frame of the dSTORM and PALM typical labels (estimate, 2026-10-07).

k_on and onSec as the microtubules' (estimate: 9-10 nt imagers, 0.05 s). imagerNm 2.5 nM (estimate, chosen 2026-10-13; was 1 nM): 2.5x the binding of 1 nM, about 2-3 pore blinks per frame over the bottom of a nucleus; the pores' docking strands sit on a SNAP- or Halo-tagged Nup96 (schlichthaerle2019, whose own imager kinetics are not modelled).

targets.name: Nuclear lamina
targets.notes: Points on the nuclear envelope (core param laminDensity per um^2, uniform by area, none within laminNpcExclNm / 2 of a pore centre): a random stand-in for the lamin network (estimate, chosen 2026-10-27). Unlabelled by default (defaultDye None): a label (<prefix>-dye, Micro-Manager CellField.NuclearLamina_Label) turns it on.

paint.notes: as the nuclear pores' (estimate: 9-10 nt imagers, 0.05 s, 2.5 nM).

specimens.name: DNA-origami nanorulers

illumination.notes: TIRF in place of a DNA-PAINT light preset's HILO: the rods lie on the coverslip; 1.03 is under the 1.40 objective's pupil edge (1.047 with water, 1.337) and gives d ~ 150 nm at 640 nm (axelrod1981); estimate (no source for the exact position).

specimens.notes: DNA-origami rods lying on a coverslip (the nanoruler: a 13 nm rod with three spots of docking strands, 80 nm apart by default, bent in-plane as a worm-like chain; or a rigid 2D origami such as the TU Delft logo (core/src/origami.*, data/origami/designs.json).

paint.notes: k_on as the microtubules' (estimate). onSec = 0.2 s / ln 2: a bound half-time of 200 ms (estimate, chosen 2026-10-12), in the order of 9 nt docking strands (~0.3-1 s mean). imagerNm 20 nM (estimate, chosen 2026-10-12): a rod with 12 strands binds every ~4 s.
